annotations.target_phrase: Descende, calve, ut ne nimium decalveris.
annotations.annotation_text: (Latin) Come down, O bald head, lest you be made excessively bald.[1]
sources: Gifford, Don, and Robert J. Seidman. Ulysses Annotated. University of California Press, 1988.

annotations.target_phrase: The fat of kidneys of wheat.
annotations.annotation_text: This is a quotation from Deuteronomy 32:13-15: "and he made him to suck honey out of the rock, and oil out of the flinty rock; Butter of kine, and milk of sheep, with fat of lambs, and rams of the breed of Bashan, and goats, with the fat of kidneys of wheat; and thou didst drink the pure blood of the grape. But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him".
sources: Gifford, Don, and Robert J. Seidman. Ulysses Annotated. University of California Press, 1988.
Wikibooks: Annotations to James Joyce's Ulysses (CC-BY-SA 4.0).

annotations.annotation_text: (Italian) O yes, certainly![7] In Italian the word for yes is usually spelt sì (or, rarely, sí). Sì certo, without the comma, means certainly.
sources: Gifford, Don, and Robert J. Seidman. Ulysses Annotated. University of California Press, 1988.
Wikibooks: Annotations to James Joyce's Ulysses (CC-BY-SA 4.0).
